intro.title: Subgrid
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive card layout using CSS Subgrid to align nested elements across multiple grid items. You will learn how Subgrid allows child grid items to inherit the grid tracks of their parent, enabling consistent alignment without complex nested grids. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid and the subgrid value for grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you through implementing Subgrid step-by-step to create a clean, aligned design.
intro.usecase: Subgrid is essential for creating complex, nested layouts that maintain consistent alignment across multiple levels, such as in dashboard interfaces where data cards, charts, and controls need to align perfectly within rows and columns. It's commonly used in product grids for e-commerce sites, where items within a category must align with filters and headers, or in admin panels where nested form fields and data tables require precise grid synchronization. By using subgrid, developers can ensure visual harmony in responsive design systems, modular UI components, and any interface requiring hierarchical layout control without manual calculations.

objectives: Implement a CSS subgrid by applying the `grid-template-rows: subgrid` property to a nested grid container.
Configure a subgrid to inherit column tracks from its parent grid using `grid-template-columns: subgrid`.
Manipulate the alignment of subgrid items by adjusting `align-items` and `justify-items` properties within the subgrid context.
Construct a multi-level layout where a subgrid nests inside another grid to create complex, aligned structures.
Update an existing CSS Grid layout by integrating subgrid to synchronize track sizing across nested elements.
Control the placement of subgrid items using explicit `grid-row` and `grid-column` values that align with the parent grid's tracks.
Initialize a subgrid within a media query to adapt track inheritance responsively across different viewport sizes.

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the base HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and write the base HTML structure that will be styled with subgrid. Start by creating a simple HTML file with a container div and nested items.
steps.hint: Begin with a basic HTML structure that includes a container element and several child elements inside it. This will be the foundation for applying CSS subgrid.

steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Subgrid Demo</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container and items here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML file with a container and nested items ready for CSS styling.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a container element with at least three child items inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a container element with multiple child items inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure isn't quite right. You need a container element with several child items inside it.

steps.title: Create the main grid container
steps.instruction: In your CSS file, define a CSS rule for a grid container class named 'grid-container' that uses grid display with 3 columns and 2 rows.
steps.hint: Use the .grid-container selector and set display: grid with grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .grid-container is defined with grid display, 3 columns, and 2 rows.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a .grid-container rule with display: grid, grid-template-columns defining 3 columns, and grid-template-rows defining 2 rows.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your .grid-container rule includes display: grid, grid-template-columns with 3 values, and grid-template-rows with 2 values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .grid-container is missing or incomplete. Ensure it uses display: grid with 3 columns and 2 rows defined.

steps.title: Style the grid items
steps.instruction: Create CSS rules for three grid items with distinct background colors and place them in specific positions within the main grid container.
steps.hint: Define classes for grid items (like .item-1, .item-2, .item-3) with background colors and use grid-column and grid-row properties to position them.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three grid items are styled with background colors and positioned within the grid container.
successCriteria: CSS rules for at least three grid items are defined with background colors and grid positioning properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some grid item styles, but make sure you have at least three items with background colors and proper positioning.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid items are not properly styled or positioned. Check that you've defined CSS rules for three items with background colors and grid-column/grid-row properties.

steps.title: Create a nested grid inside a grid item
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a nested grid container inside one of the main grid items. Use a class selector like '.nested-grid' and set display: grid with grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule after your existing grid item styles. The selector should target a class you'll add to an HTML element later.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for a nested grid container is created, preparing for the next step where you'll apply it to a grid item.
successCriteria: A CSS rule with a class selector (like '.nested-grid') exists with display: grid and grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your rule includes both 'display: grid' and 'grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested grid rule isn't quite right. Remember to create a new CSS rule with a class selector that sets up a grid with two columns.

steps.title: Style the nested grid items
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the items inside your nested grid container. Create a selector for the nested grid items and give them a background color and padding.
steps.hint: You can target the items inside your nested grid using a descendant selector like '.nested-grid-item' or a class you define. Set properties like background-color and padding to make them visually distinct.
steps.expectedOutcome: The nested grid items will have distinct styling with background color and padding, making them visible within the nested grid.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for nested grid items is added with at least background-color and padding properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include both background-color and padding properties for the nested grid items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested grid items are not properly styled. Check that you've created a CSS rule for them with background-color and padding.

steps.title: Introduce the subgrid property
steps.instruction: In the nested grid rule, replace the explicit grid definition with 'subgrid' for both columns and rows to inherit the parent grid's tracks.
steps.hint: Change the 'grid-template-columns' and 'grid-template-rows' properties to use the value 'subgrid' instead of explicit track sizes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The nested grid will now inherit the column and row tracks from its parent grid container.
successCriteria: The nested grid rule includes 'grid-template-columns: subgrid' and 'grid-template-rows: subgrid'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both 'grid-template-columns' and 'grid-template-rows' are set to 'subgrid'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested grid should use 'subgrid' for both columns and rows instead of explicit track definitions.

steps.title: Apply subgrid to columns
steps.instruction: In your nested grid rule, set grid-template-columns to subgrid to align its columns with the parent grid.
steps.hint: Add grid-template-columns: subgrid; to the CSS rule for your nested grid container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The nested grid will inherit its column tracks from the parent grid container.
successCriteria: The nested grid rule includes grid-template-columns: subgrid;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added grid-template-columns: subgrid; to your nested grid rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. The step requires setting grid-template-columns to subgrid in your nested grid CSS rule.

steps.title: Apply subgrid to rows
steps.instruction: In your nested grid container rule, add the property grid-template-rows: subgrid; to align its rows with the parent grid's rows.
steps.hint: This property makes the nested grid inherit the row tracks from its parent grid container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The nested grid container will now have its rows aligned with the parent grid's rows using subgrid.
successCriteria: The nested grid container rule includes grid-template-rows: subgrid;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added grid-template-rows: subgrid; to the nested grid container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the correct property to the nested grid container. The property should be grid-template-rows: subgrid;

steps.title: Position items within the subgrid
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to position the nested grid items (.nested-item) within the subgrid container to align with the parent grid's column and row lines.
steps.hint: Use grid-column and grid-row properties on the .nested-item class to place items in specific grid cells of the subgrid.
steps.expectedOutcome: The nested grid items will be positioned within the subgrid container, aligning with the parent grid's column and row tracks.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .nested-item include grid-column and grid-row properties to position items within the subgrid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both grid-column and grid-row properties to position the items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested items aren't positioned correctly. Check that you've added grid-column and grid-row properties to the .nested-item class.

steps.title: Add visual styling to demonstrate alignment
steps.instruction: Add background colors and borders to the grid items and nested grid items to visually highlight how subgrid creates perfect alignment between parent and child grids.
steps.hint: Use background-color and border properties on your existing grid item and nested grid item selectors to create visual distinction.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid items and nested grid items will have distinct background colors and borders, making the alignment created by subgrid clearly visible.
successCriteria: Background colors and borders are applied to both grid items and nested grid items to visually demonstrate subgrid alignment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both grid items and nested grid items have distinct background colors and borders to fully demonstrate the alignment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visual styling is missing or incomplete. Add background colors and borders to both grid items and nested grid items to highlight the subgrid alignment.
